TITLE: Audit and attack the L8 exact-rank factor claim
QUESTION: Under the stated Pell/Lucas framework, does every relevant prime factor of Q_q = P_(q^2)/P_q have exact rank q^2, and do q = 47, 71, 83 yield reproducible witnesses when Q_q is factored?

CHECKS.DESCRIPTION: Derive the L8 implication from standard Lucas/Pell divisibility and rank properties, stating all exceptional-prime and valuation assumptions explicitly.
Factor Q_47, Q_71 and Q_83 as far as practical while recording complete or partial factorization status separately.
For every prime factor found, independently compute its Pell entry rank and test whether the rank is exactly q^2 rather than a proper divisor.
Reproduce the reported bounded k scan and preserve its exact interval, candidate count and zero-witness result without converting that result into a non-existence proof.

CONFIRMATION_CRITERIA: The source audit proves the implication with all required exceptions stated.
At least one independently verified prime factor for a target q has exact Pell rank q^2.
The reproduced bounded scan agrees on its exact search interval and reports 4853 prime candidates with zero exact witnesses under the same protocol.
CONTRADICTION_CRITERIA: A prime factor of Q_q satisfying the stated domain assumptions has Pell rank strictly smaller than q^2.
The source audit reveals an unstated exceptional case that invalidates the universal wording of L8.
Independent reproduction changes the reported bounded-scan candidate count or finds an exact witness inside the same scanned interval.
A claimed factorization witness cannot be reproduced from the recorded Q_q.
NOTES: L8 remains a derived relation under audit, not a novelty claim.
Partial factorization must never be reported as complete factorization.
